summary.text: Joseline Peña-Melnyk is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 21, where she has served since January 10, 2007. The House unanimously elected her Speaker on December 16, 2025, and she is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.

paragraphs.text: Peña-Melnyk was born in the Dominican Republic in 1966.
She received a bachelor's degree in criminal justice from Buffalo State College in 1987 and a law degree from the University at Buffalo School of Law in 1991.
She worked as an attorney with the Defender Association of Philadelphia from 1991 to 1992 and as an assistant U.S. attorney in the District of Columbia from 1997 to 1999.
Peña-Melnyk was first elected to public office in 2003, winning a seat on the College Park city council, on which she served until 2006.
In 2006 she was elected to the Maryland House of Delegates as one of three Democrats elected in District 21.
She chaired the House Health and Government Operations Committee and was a founding member of the Maryland Legislative Latino Caucus, which she chaired from 2014 to 2017.
When elected Speaker, she was described by Ballotpedia as the first immigrant and Afro-Latina to hold that office in the state's history.
